record.paper_title: Heavy flavors and quarkonia: highlights, open questions, and perspectives
record.original_question: Do charm hypernuclei exist, and what Λc+-p interaction potential binds or fails to bind a Λc+ baryon to ordinary matter? More specifically, can Λc+-p femtoscopic correlation measurements in pp and heavy-ion collisions calibrate the Λc+-p potential, discriminate between lattice-QCD and phenomenological potentials, and confirm or rule out Λc+-p bound states despite Coulomb repulsion?

evidence.quote: The little experimental knowledge available about the charm hadron’s strong interactions hinders progress in the long-standing issue regarding the existence of charm hypernuclei.
A first measurement of Λ+c-p interactions would be important to calibrate the strength of the potential responsible for binding the Λ+c baryon to ordinary matter.

In general, the phenomenological models suggest a more strongly attractive Λ+c-p force than lQCD, and some even lead to two-body bound states. The bound states predicted survive despite of the Coulomb repulsion.

The delicate interplay between the repulsive Coulomb interaction and the strongly attractive Λ+c-p potential produces a distinct dependence on the source radius and this characteristic behaviour constitutes an extremely useful signature that will help for either confirming or ruling out such bound states in experiments.
It is safe to say that even an experiment with moderate statistics will be sufficient to discriminate among the calculations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the charmed baryon Λc+ (a hadron consisting of an up, down, and charm quark with electric charge +1) interacting with a proton p. Two classes of Λc+–p interaction potentials are commonly proposed: (i) potentials derived from lattice QCD calculations, which tend to be moderately attractive, and (ii) phenomenological meson-exchange potentials, which tend to be more strongly attractive and in some cases admit a two-body Λc+–p bound state surviving the repulsive Coulomb interaction between the two positively charged baryons.

(a) Determine whether charm hypernuclei — nuclei containing at least one bound Λc+ baryon together with ordinary nucleons — exist as quantum-mechanically bound systems, and characterize the Λc+–nucleon potential that would bind a Λc+ to ordinary nuclear matter.

(b) For the two-body system specifically, decide whether the Λc+–p system supports a bound state once the attractive strong interaction and the repulsive Coulomb interaction are both included.

(c) Show whether femtoscopic two-particle correlation functions C(k*) of Λc+–p pairs, measured in high-energy pp and heavy-ion collisions as a function of the relative momentum k* and the emitting source radius, can quantitatively calibrate the Λc+–p interaction potential and discriminate between lattice-QCD-based and phenomenological potentials, in particular by exploiting the predicted source-radius dependence induced by the interplay of Coulomb repulsion and strong attraction.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent ALICE femtoscopy measurements of Λc+–p correlations in pp collisions at the LHC have begun to constrain the interaction, with preliminary Run 3 results disfavoring (at roughly 1σ) the most strongly attractive phenomenological potentials and hence the formation of Λc+–p bound states, but the existence of charm hypernuclei and a definitive discrimination between lattice-QCD and phenomenological Λc+–N potentials remain unresolved. Higher-statistics measurements and ALICE 3 are explicitly identified as needed to settle the question.

status_evidence.title: Probing the strong interaction between charm hadrons and charged particles with femtoscopy measurements with ALICE
status_evidence.snippet: With the upgraded ITS 2 and increased Run 3 luminosity, ALICE explores charm baryon–proton interactions; preliminary Λc+–p results at ~1σ would, if confirmed, disfavor the formation of charmed hypernuclei. ALICE 3 will enable charmed hypernuclei reconstruction.
status_evidence.claim: Charm hypernuclei existence and Λc+–p bound state are still being investigated; current femtoscopy data are inconclusive but tend to disfavor strongly attractive phenomenological potentials.

status_evidence.title: Hadron Physics Opportunities at FAIR
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open questions on charm-baryon nucleon interactions and the search for charmed hypernuclei as a future research program.
status_evidence.claim: Charm hypernuclei remain an open experimental and theoretical target for future facilities.
